main.title: Resistance 2
main.subtitle: The invasion crosses the Atlantic
main.summary: Resistance 2 is Insomniac Games' PlayStation 3 first-person shooter, released in North America on 4 November 2008. Nathan Hale returns to fight the Chimera as their invasion reaches the United States. Now part of the Sentinels, he serves alongside other soldiers infected with the same virus and dependent on inhibitors to restrain it. The campaign moves through recognisable American locations transformed by alien occupation. Its larger battles and enormous opponents expand the scale of the original game's alternate-history war, while Hale's condition continues to threaten him from within.

cards.heading: The invasion crosses the Atlantic
cards.text: Resistance 2 is Insomniac Games' PlayStation 3 first-person shooter, released in North America on 4 November 2008. Nathan Hale returns to fight the Chimera as their invasion reaches the United States. Now part of the Sentinels, he serves alongside other soldiers infected with the same virus and dependent on inhibitors to restrain it. The campaign moves through recognisable American locations transformed by alien occupation. Its larger battles and enormous opponents expand the scale of the original game's alternate-history war, while Hale's condition continues to threaten him from within.

cards.heading: Choose what to carry into the next fight
cards.text: The campaign limits Hale to two carried weapons, asking the player to change equipment as the situation changes. Conventional-looking firearms share space with the series' stranger Chimeran designs, whose alternate functions can alter the way an encounter is approached. Health recovery and the available cover shape the pace of moving between attacks. Some enemies fill the landscape rather than behaving like another soldier in a corridor. These encounters emphasise the invasion's scale, turning a familiar street or skyline into the setting for a much larger threat.

cards.heading: A separate war fought together
cards.text: Alongside the campaign, Resistance 2 introduced an eight-player cooperative mode built around complementary soldier classes and separate objectives. Competitive multiplayer supported much larger groups, making online play a major part of the release's identity. The division gave players several ways to return to the same war rather than simply replaying Hale's story. Critics praised its ambition and presentation, although changes from the first game divided players. Sony closed the online servers in April 2014. Resistance 3 continued the setting in 2011 with a more personal journey through its aftermath.

main.title: Gears of War 2
main.summary: Gears of War 2 is a 2008 third-person shooter video game developed by Epic Games and published by Microsoft Game Studios for the Xbox 360.

cards.heading: Delta Squad returns
cards.text: Gears of War 2 is a 2008 third-person shooter video game developed by Epic Games and published by Microsoft Game Studios for the Xbox 360. It is the second installment of the Gears of War series, with lead design by Cliff Bleszinski. The game was released in North America, Europe and Australia on November 7, 2008, and was released in Japan on July 30, 2009. The game expands technically on the previous game by using a modified Unreal Engine 3. The development team brought in comic book writer Joshua Ortega to help write the plot for the game.

cards.heading: The underground assault and Horde
cards.text: In Gears of War 2, the COG continues its fight against the Locust, who are attempting to sink all of the cities on the planet Sera. Sergeant Marcus Fenix leads Delta Squad into the depths of the planet to try to stop the Locust during the assault upon Locust territory. The player controls Fenix in the main mission campaign, with the ability to play cooperatively with a second player controlling Fenix's best friend and fellow Squad member Dominic "Dom" Santiago. The game includes several existing and new multiplayer modes including five-on-five battles between human and Locust forces, and a "Horde" mode that challenges up to five players against waves of Locust forces with ever-increasing strength. New weapons and gameplay mechanics such as "chainsaw duels" and the ability to use downed foes as "meatshields" were added to the game.

cards.heading: Reception and Gears of War 3
cards.text: On its release weekend, Gears of War 2 sold over two million copies, and within two months of release, had sold four million copies. It was the seventh best selling video game of 2009 and received several accolades. The game received similar praise as its predecessor, with the new gameplay and multiplayer modes seen as outstanding additions. Gears of War 2, along with its predecessor, are considered to be amongst the best games ever made. It was followed by Gears of War 3 in 2011.

main.title: Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts & Bolts
main.subtitle: Build the move you need
main.summary: Rare’s 2008 Xbox 360 adventure makes vehicle construction central to Banjo and Kazooie’s contest with Gruntilda: the next useful ability can be something the player builds.

cards.heading: An adventure assembled from parts
cards.text: Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts & Bolts was released in 2008 for Xbox 360, developed by Rare and published by Microsoft Game Studios. L.O.G. turns the struggle over Spiral Mountain into a series of challenges. Rather than relying only on an expanding set of character moves, players assemble vehicles from parts: wheels, engines, wings and other components become tools for crossing terrain, carrying objects and reaching goals. A challenge sets the destination; the machine is the player’s answer.

cards.heading: From the town to the workshop
cards.text: Showdown Town connects the adventure to Mumbo’s Motors, where designs can be built, tested and saved as blueprints. Speed, weight and the arrangement of parts make construction part of the puzzle rather than a purely decorative activity. The game retains Banjo’s characters and humour while changing how their abilities are obtained. Its orchestral score also draws on that history: Grant Kirkhope worked with Robin Beanland and David Clynick, bringing familiar musical references into the new mechanical playground.

main.title: Call of Duty: World at War
main.subtitle: Two fronts and the beginning of Zombies
main.summary: Treyarch returns to the Second World War with Pacific and Eastern Front campaigns, cooperative missions and the first Call of Duty Zombies mode.

cards.heading: The Pacific and Eastern Fronts
cards.text: Call of Duty: World at War first appeared in North America on 11 November 2008. Developed by Treyarch and published by Activision, the main game was released for Windows, PlayStation 3, Xbox 360 and Wii. Its campaign follows American Marines fighting Japanese forces in the Pacific and Soviet soldiers advancing against Germany on the Eastern Front. Built on the Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare engine, it combines infantry battles with vehicles and airborne missions. The PlayStation 2 game Final Fronts and the Nintendo DS edition were separate productions rather than identical versions of this campaign.

cards.heading: A campaign for four players
cards.text: For the first time in the series, the main campaign supports cooperative play with up to four players online on Windows, PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360. Players can move through the missions together, help one another survive and compete for points in Competitive Co-Op. The environments also change the rhythm of combat: concealed Japanese troops launch ambushes and close-range charges, while a flamethrower can set nearby vegetation alight. Cooperation takes place within these scripted battles rather than in a separate sequence of multiplayer arenas.

cards.heading: Classes, perks and tanks online
cards.text: Competitive multiplayer develops the class-based structure introduced by Modern Warfare. Players earn experience, rise through ranks, unlock weapons and equip perks to shape their loadouts. Persistent statistics and challenges give matches a progression beyond a single round. Tanks add vehicle combat to some battlefields, placing infantry and armour in the same encounter. These systems carry the series' recent online design back into Second World War settings instead of returning to the simpler multiplayer rules of the earlier games.

cards.heading: Surviving Nacht der Untoten
cards.text: World at War also introduces the series' Zombies survival mode on Windows, PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360; it is absent from the Wii edition. Completing the campaign originally leads into Nacht der Untoten, a ruined building defended against successive waves of undead attackers. Up to four players begin with limited equipment and earn points by fighting zombies and repairing barricades. Those points buy weapons and open additional rooms, while fallen teammates can be revived before everyone is overwhelmed. The original map has neither the perk machines nor the weapon-upgrade machine added in later maps: its appeal rests on a compact space, scarce resources and the attempt to survive one more round.

main.title: Mirror's Edge
main.summary: Mirror's Edge is a 2008 first-person action-adventure platform game developed by DICE and published by Electronic Arts.

cards.heading: Faith crosses the city
cards.text: Mirror's Edge is a 2008 first-person action-adventure platform game developed by DICE and published by Electronic Arts. The game was released for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in November 2008, and for Windows in January 2009. Set in a near-future city, it follows the story of Faith Connors, an underground parkour courier who transmits messages while evading government surveillance. To progress through the game, the player must control Faith from a first-person perspective and complete a series of levels that involve performing a sequence of acrobatic maneuvers, including jumping between rooftops, running across walls, and sliding down zip lines. The game is an action-adventure game with platform and first-person shooter mechanics.

cards.heading: Movement, colour and music
cards.text: Inspired by chase scenes featured in Casino Royale and the Bourne films, Mirror's Edge features hundreds of first-person animations to convey Faith's movement and interactions with the environment. The game is powered by Unreal Engine 3, but a new lighting solution was created to better reflect colors, create soft shadows, and give the game a unique art style. The game deliberately makes use of strong primary colors, with outdoor environments predominantly featuring white and distinctively lacking in green. The game was written by Rhianna Pratchett, and its score was composed by electronic music artist Solar Fields, while the main theme song was composed by Swedish producers Rami Yacoub and Arnthor Birgisson and performed by Swedish musician Lisa Miskovsky.

cards.heading: Reception and Catalyst
cards.text: Upon release, Mirror's Edge received generally positive reviews from critics, who praised its visuals and immersive first-person perspective, but criticized its trial and error gameplay, combat mechanics, and restrictive levels. The game sold around 2.5 million units by June 2013, and won Adventure Game of the Year at the 2009 Interactive Achievement Awards. Retrospectively, Mirror's Edge has grown in esteem and developed a passionate fanbase due to its strong aesthetics and innovative game design. A prequel to the game, also titled Mirror's Edge, was released for mobile devices in 2010. A reboot that explores a new origin story for Faith, titled Mirror's Edge Catalyst, was released in 2016.

main.title: Naruto: The Broken Bond
main.subtitle: The story continues through a wider cast
main.summary: Naruto: The Broken Bond is Ubisoft Montreal's Xbox 360 action-adventure, released in North America on 18 November 2008. It continues Rise of a Ninja through the Search for Tsunade and Sasuke Retrieval story arcs. Exploration and one-on-one combat remain connected, but the sequel adds a tag-team system and a larger playable cast. The player travels through environments designed to feel richer and more densely inhabited, meeting a greater variety of characters between major confrontations. Naruto's developing relationships give the journey its direction as the story moves towards the broken bond of the title.

cards.heading: The story continues through a wider cast
cards.text: Naruto: The Broken Bond is Ubisoft Montreal's Xbox 360 action-adventure, released in North America on 18 November 2008. It continues Rise of a Ninja through the Search for Tsunade and Sasuke Retrieval story arcs. Exploration and one-on-one combat remain connected, but the sequel adds a tag-team system and a larger playable cast. The player travels through environments designed to feel richer and more densely inhabited, meeting a greater variety of characters between major confrontations. Naruto's developing relationships give the journey its direction as the story moves towards the broken bond of the title.

cards.heading: The team changes the possibilities of a fight
cards.text: The tag-team system broadens the combat beyond the abilities of one selected fighter. A larger roster allows different combinations to enter a contest, while adjustments to the fighting system build on the first game's approach. Outside battles, the adventure retains the importance of exploring the environment and moving through the world between story events. Improved lighting and a more painterly visual treatment help distinguish those places. The player alternates between navigating the setting and concentrating on a confrontation, with the available team providing another way to express the relationships already central to the anime.

cards.heading: A second adaptation refines the visual continuity
cards.text: The sequel replaces the earlier game's borrowed anime scenes with three-dimensional cinematics, keeping story sequences closer to the visual form of the playable adventure. Original anime voices and music maintain another connection to the source. Online competition receives a revised ranking system, while the expanded cast provides more choices for local contests. It was Ubisoft's second and final Naruto game before its licence expired. The Broken Bond develops the earlier adaptation's central attraction: a familiar animated world that can be explored between fights, with the cast and its changing loyalties shaping both parts of the experience.

main.title: Left 4 Dead
main.summary: Left 4 Dead is a 2008 first-person shooter game developed by Valve South and published by Valve.

cards.heading: Four survivors against the infected
cards.text: Left 4 Dead is a 2008 first-person shooter game developed by Valve South and published by Valve. It was originally released for Windows and Xbox 360 in November 2008 and for Mac OS X in October 2010, and is the first title in the Left 4 Dead series. Set during the aftermath of a zombie outbreak on the East Coast of the United States, the game pits its four protagonists, dubbed the "Survivors", against hordes of the infected.

cards.heading: The Director shapes each attempt
cards.text: Left 4 Dead uses Valve's proprietary Source engine, with four game modes: a single-player mode in which allied characters are controlled by AI, a four-player co-op campaign mode, an eight-player online versus mode, and a four-player survival mode. In all modes, an artificial intelligence dubbed the "Director" controls level pacing and item placements in an attempt to create a dynamic experience and increase replay value.

cards.heading: Cooperation and a sequel
cards.text: Left 4 Dead received praise for its replay value, focus on cooperative play, and cinematic feel, although some criticized its limited level selection and lack of narrative. Considered one of the greatest video games ever made, the game won several publication awards, as well as distinctions from the Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences and British Academy of Film and Television Arts. As was done with Team Fortress 2, Valve supplemented the game with free downloadable content. The success of the game led to the development of the sequel Left 4 Dead 2, which was released in 2009. In 2012, all Left 4 Dead campaigns were ported to Left 4 Dead 2, with cross-platform multiplayer support between Windows and Mac versions of the game.

main.title: LocoRoco 2
main.subtitle: New ways to move, new voices to discover
main.summary: The original PSP sequel keeps the tilting world and adds underwater travel, musical challenges and a home built for rescued MuiMui.

cards.heading: A song threatens the LocoRoco planet
cards.text: LocoRoco 2 first appeared on PSP in Europe on 21 November 2008. Sony Computer Entertainment’s sequel returns to a world whose inhabitants had recovered from the Moja invasion. Their enemy Bon Mucho now has a song that drains the life from living things. The LocoRoco must restore their planet while facing the returning Moja and new characters, including the purple LocoRoco Viole.

cards.heading: Swimming, swinging and rolling inside shells
cards.text: The player still controls the planet rather than directly steering a creature. The shoulder buttons tilt the landscape, and pressing both makes the LocoRoco jump. Pressing ○ separates a large LocoRoco into smaller ones; holding ○ gathers them together again. The sequel extends this familiar movement with swimming, swinging and shells that can carry the creatures through enemies or obstacles. A later super jump opens routes that were previously out of reach.

cards.heading: Musical challenges within the journey
cards.text: Music also becomes part of the journey’s challenges. During musical minigames, the player performs along with the scene to earn notes. The cheerful voices are joined by the Moja’s darker sounds, making encounters part of the changing musical world. These sequences sit within the adventure rather than replacing the rolling, exploring and collecting that define the series.

cards.heading: Building a home for the MuiMui
cards.text: The MuiMui House gives rescued inhabitants a place to live. It starts as an empty shell, and items collected across the stages can be used to build rooms, furniture and toys. As more MuiMui arrive, the house provides another reason to revisit levels and search for useful objects. Its growing collection of spaces and activities turns progress through the world into a home the player can gradually furnish.

main.title: Patapon 2
main.subtitle: A masked hero joins the rhythm-led army
main.summary: The original PSP sequel expands Patapon's musical strategy with new troops, a customizable Hero and four-player cooperation. Commands still depend on keeping a steady drumbeat.

cards.heading: A new land beyond the shipwreck
cards.text: Patapon 2 first reached the PSP in Japan on 27 November 2008. Developed by Pyramid and Japan Studio and published by Sony Computer Entertainment, it continues the tribe's search for Earthend after a shipwreck leaves it in unfamiliar territory. The player remains its unseen deity, using rhythmic drum commands to direct the tiny warriors against the Karmen tribe and the creatures of this new land.

cards.heading: Keeping the army in Fever
cards.text: Each face button represents a talking drum. Sequences played on the beat tell the army to march, attack, defend or retreat. Mistimed or unrecognized commands interrupt its actions, while accurate repeated patterns bring the warriors into Fever and improve their fighting abilities. Before a mission, the player arranges troops and equips weapons and armor; returning to earlier battles supplies materials and equipment for the next challenge.

cards.heading: A Hero with changing classes and masks
cards.text: The Hero Patapon adds a powerful, customizable warrior to the army. It can adopt an unlocked class and wear masks that change its attributes, while well-timed commands in Fever activate special abilities. An evolution tree also opens new possibilities for the other troops. Bird-riding Toripons, large-fisted Robopons and magic-using Mahopons give the player more ways to assemble a force rather than merely increasing the number of identical soldiers.

cards.heading: Four Heroes carry an egg together
cards.text: The PSP edition introduces local ad hoc cooperation for four Hero Patapons. Through the Patagate, players carry a mysterious egg across a dangerous battlefield and then drum together to hatch it, earning masks and other rewards. Game Sharing lets friends join even if only one person owns the game, and computer-controlled ComPons fill empty places. Cooperation therefore asks each participant to keep time while protecting a shared objective, rather than simply following the single-player army.

main.title: Professor Layton and the Unwound Future
main.subtitle: A letter from an older Luke
main.summary: Professor Layton and the Unwound Future is Level-5's third Nintendo DS puzzle adventure, known as Lost Future in Europe. Layton encounters an older version of Luke who asks for help with a disastrous future. The premise turns an established partnership into a mystery about what time may do to familiar people. Exploration still moves through illustrated locations and conversations, with puzzles interrupting the investigation. The prospect of a changed London gives those ordinary actions a more personal question: which parts of the world, and of its people, can be trusted?

cards.heading: A letter from an older Luke
cards.text: Professor Layton and the Unwound Future is Level-5's third Nintendo DS puzzle adventure, known as Lost Future in Europe. Layton encounters an older version of Luke who asks for help with a disastrous future. The premise turns an established partnership into a mystery about what time may do to familiar people. Exploration still moves through illustrated locations and conversations, with puzzles interrupting the investigation. The prospect of a changed London gives those ordinary actions a more personal question: which parts of the world, and of its people, can be trusted?

cards.heading: One more hint when it matters
cards.text: The puzzles range across logic, visual reasoning and mathematics, with no time limit for reaching an answer. Hint coins buy successive clues, and this instalment adds a stronger Super Hint after the ordinary three have been revealed. Choosing assistance can therefore be a gradual decision rather than an immediate surrender of the solution. Tapping the scenery also uncovers coins and hidden puzzles. The illustrated streets remain worth examining, while the hint system leaves room for readers with different levels of patience or experience to follow the same mystery.

cards.heading: Small stories inside the trunk
cards.text: Additional activities include arranging stickers into a coherent story, guiding a toy car with directional markers and helping a parrot carry objects along a route. Each gives a familiar object another set of spatial rules to solve. The trunk also preserves completed puzzles and information about the investigation, making it a useful place to return between locations. These quieter tasks sit beside the larger uncertainty of the future. The adventure's emotional scale can grow while its ordinary pleasures remain those of noticing, arranging and finally understanding a small problem.
